request.spec:
A person can have plans: an amount, a start date, every N days (a whole number, at least 1) and an
end date, from a form on the row (PLAN_ADDED name=<name> amount=<amount> start=<date>
every=<n> end=<date>; an end before the start or a bad amount or interval is refused with an error
on the row). A generate button on the screen makes, for every plan on the sheet in the order they
were added, a DRAFT claim with the plan's amount for every plan date (the start, then every N days)
up to the end and the sheet's today that has none yet, dated that day with an empty note, by the
claim form's rules (a date the form refuses is skipped and tried again next time). Show how many
were made, and on each plan how many claims it has made so far.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person can have plans: an amount, a start date, every N days (a whole number, at least 1) and an
end date, from a form on the row (PLAN_ADDED name=<name> amount=<amount> start=<date>
every=<n> end=<date>; an end before the start or a bad amount or interval is refused with an error
on the row). A generate button on the screen makes, for every plan on the sheet in the order they
were added, a DRAFT claim with the plan's amount for every plan date (the start, then every N days)
up to the end and the sheet's today that has none yet, dated that day with an empty note, by the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now have plans, and a generate button makes their draft claims. `bin/e2e` passes all four tests in the spec on the first full run.

**Stored data** (`V67__plan.sql`)
- A `plan` table holds each plan: its person, amount, start, every N days and end.
- A `plan_claim` table records which plan dates already have a claim, and which claim it was. That gives "has none yet", and it also gives each plan's made-so-far count.

**Server** (new `plan` package, all endpoints under `/api/`)
- `POST /people/{personId}/plans` adds a plan. It is refused (400, nothing stored, nothing audited) when:
  - the amount isn't 0.00 or more with up to two decimals,
  - every N days isn't a whole number of at least 1,
  - a date doesn't parse, or the end is before the start.
- A plan that goes through writes `PLAN_ADDED … name= amount= start= every= end=`.
- `GET /plans` lists the sheet's plans, each with how many claims it has made.
- `POST /generate-plans` goes through every plan in the order they were added. For each plan date (the start, then every N days, up to the end and the sheet's today) that has no claim yet, it builds a DRAFT claim with the plan's amount and an empty note.
  - It builds that claim with the same rules the claim form uses. A date those rules refuse (closed period, after retirement) is skipped and nothing is recorded for it, so it is tried again next time.
  - Each claim it makes is audited and logged exactly as a claim from the form would be. The response is how many it made.

**Front end** (`features/plans/`)
- Each person's row has a Plans cell. It lists that person's plans as `plan-row-<id>`, with `plan-generated` showing the count. It also holds the add form and its `plan-error`, which clears when a field changes or the next action on the row is taken.
- A screen-level panel holds the `plan-generate` button and `plan-generated-count`. The count is gone while it runs, and shows again once it's done. There's also a `plan-generate-error`.

A plan whose person is no longer on the sheet (moved or merged away) is skipped. The request didn't say what should happen in that case.
